title: Group including 49ers minority owner agrees to buy Seahawks for what is said to be record price
content:
A group led by the Khosla family, including San Francisco 49ers minority owner Vinod Khosla, reached an agreement to buy the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, the estate of Paul Allen announced Saturday.

The purchase price is $9.612 billion, league sources granted anonymity to discuss the confidential matter told The Athletic. The sale is subject to the approval of NFL owners, and if confirmed, would establish a record price for an NFL franchise.

“We are honored to be entrusted as the next stewards of the Seattle Seahawks. We look forward to building on the winning legacy Paul Allen created and to earning the trust of the Seahawks organization and fans everywhere,” Vinod Khosla, on behalf of the Khosla family, said in a statement.

According to a memo the NFL sent to chief executives and club presidents and obtained by The Athletic, the Khosla family includes Neeru Khosla, who would serve as the controlling owner; Vinod Khosla, who purchased a minority share of the 49ers last year; and their son Neal Khosla.

The NFL describes Neeru Khosla as an educator and entrepreneur. Vinod Khosla co-founded Sun Microsystems. Neal Khosla is the CEO of Curai, an AI healthcare company and “would be expected to have a significant leadership role in the ownership group,” the memo said.

The memo noted that the Khosla family must divest its interest in the 49ers.

The current record price was recorded when the Washington Commanders were sold for $6.05 billion to a group led by private equity investor Josh Harris in 2023.

The Commanders’ sale process took more than eight months from the time former owner Daniel Snyder announced he was considering selling to the time the deal closed. The Denver Broncos, held in a trust established by former owner Pat Bowlen, were sold in 2022 to the Walton-Penner family for $4.65 billion after a relatively swift four-month process.

Allen’s estate announced it had begun the formal sale process of the franchise 10 days after the Seahawks defeated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl 60. That was the franchise’s second Super Bowl win of the Allen family’s nearly three decades of control. Seattle also boasts four NFC championships and 11 division titles during the span.

Allen, who served as controlling owner until his death in October 2018 at 65 from non-Hodgkin lymphoma, bought the franchise from Ken Behring for roughly $200 million in 1997 and prevented the team from leaving Seattle. Behring had planned to move the team to Anaheim, Calif.
